name: Whey Classic
short: The one you reach for every day. 24 g protein, mixes in five seconds, tastes like it should.
description: Whey Classic is a concentrate-based whey with 24 g of protein per scoop and nothing clever going on. It dissolves in water with a spoon, it does not foam up the shaker, and the chocolate is chocolate — not "chocolate flavour". This is the tub that lives on your counter and gets used twice a day for a year.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml water or milk. Straight after training, or whenever the day left you short on protein.

name: Whey Classic
short: Vanilla that stays out of the way. Blends with fruit, oats and coffee without fighting them.
description: Same whey, quieter flavour. Vanilla is the one to buy if you put protein in porridge, in a smoothie, or in your morning coffee — it carries whatever you mix it with instead of shouting over it. 24 g protein per scoop, 33 scoops in the tub.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml water or milk. Also stirs straight into yoghurt or oats.

name: Whey Classic
short: Light, cold, done. The one people drink in summer when chocolate feels heavy.
description: Strawberry Whey Classic with 24 g protein per scoop. Best in cold water rather than milk — it stays light and drinks like a shake instead of a dessert. Same concentrate base as the rest of the Classic line.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml ice-cold water. Shake hard, drink within the hour.

name: Whey Classic
short: Banana and oats, the oldest breakfast in the gym. 24 g protein per scoop.
description: If your first meal is a blender, this is the tub for it: banana whey, 40 g oats, a handful of ice. 24 g protein per scoop, no gritty finish, and it does not turn grey the way real banana does.
usage: One scoop (30 g) with oats and 300 ml milk. Blend, drink, get on with the day.

name: Whey Classic
short: Two months of chocolate whey at €0,83 a shake. The size most people settle on.
description: The 2 kg bag of Whey Classic Chocolate — 66 servings, same formula as the 1 kg tub, about a fifth cheaper per shake. Resealable bag, not a bucket, so it fits in a normal kitchen cupboard.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml water or milk. Scoop included, buried somewhere in the bag.

name: Whey Classic
short: 66 servings of the flavour that mixes into anything without taking over.
description: Vanilla Whey Classic in the 2 kg bag. Buy this one if you use protein in cooking as much as in shakes — vanilla goes into pancakes, quark and overnight oats without a fight. 24 g protein per scoop.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml liquid, or fold a scoop through 250 g quark.

name: Whey Classic bulk
short: 100 shakes. The cheapest protein per gram we sell, and it takes a shelf.
description: Three kilos of Whey Classic Chocolate — a hundred servings at €0,79 a shake. This is the bag for a household with two lifters or one very consistent one. Store it dry and clip it shut; three kilos is a long relationship.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml water or milk, two to three times a day if you are training hard.

name: Whey Starter
short: A small tub to find out whether you actually like it. Two weeks’ worth.
description: Whey Starter is the 500 g tub for a first protein purchase: 22 g per scoop, sixteen servings, under twenty euro. Buy it, drink it for two weeks, then decide whether white chocolate is your flavour before you commit to three kilos of it.
usage: One scoop (28 g) in 250 ml water or milk, once a day on top of normal meals.

name: Whey Starter
short: Sweet, with actual biscuit pieces. Our best-selling first tub.
description: Cookies & cream with real biscuit pieces through it, in the small 500 g size. It is the flavour that gets people to finish the tub, which is the only thing a first protein has to do. 22 g protein per scoop.
usage: One scoop (28 g) in 250 ml milk. Water works, milk is better for this one.

name: Whey Isolate
short: 27 g protein, under 0,5 g lactose, no heaviness afterwards.
description: Filtered further than concentrate, so you get more protein and almost no lactose or fat: 27 g protein per 30 g scoop, under 0,5 g lactose. Buy this if normal whey sits badly with you, or if you are counting the last few grams of a cut.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml water. Isolate is thin by design — do not expect a milkshake.

name: Whey Isolate
short: Clean vanilla isolate. 27 g protein, 108 kcal, almost no lactose.
description: The vanilla version of our isolate: 27 g protein and 108 kcal per serving, under 0,5 g lactose. Light enough to drink twice a day without feeling like you ate something, which is the point of an isolate.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml cold water, before or after training.

name: Whey Isolate bulk
short: Sixty isolate shakes. For people who already know isolate is what they want.
description: 1,8 kg of chocolate isolate — sixty servings at €1,32 each, against €1,50 in the small tub. Not a first purchase. Buy it when you have already worked out that concentrate does not agree with you.
usage: One scoop (30 g) in 250 ml water, once or twice a day.

name: Pure Whey Isolate
short: One ingredient. No sweetener, no flavouring, no colour. 28 g protein per scoop.
description: Whey protein isolate and nothing else. No sucralose, no stevia, no aroma — which is why it costs more than the flavoured line rather than less: an unflavoured powder has nowhere to hide, so the protein has to be good on its own. Faintly milky, slightly salty, disappears completely into food.
usage: One scoop (30 g) into porridge, quark, soup or a smoothie. Straight in water is honest but joyless.

name: Pure Whey Concentrate
short: Unflavoured concentrate for people who cook with their protein.
description: The same concentrate as Whey Classic with the flavour system taken out: whey and whey alone. It bakes better than isolate — it keeps things moist — so this is the tub for protein pancakes, banana bread and anything that goes in an oven. No sweeteners of any kind.
usage: Swap 30 g of flour for 30 g of this in a bake, or stir a scoop through 250 g quark.

name: Vegan Protein
short: Pea and rice, blended so the amino profile is complete. 22 g per scoop.
description: Pea and brown rice protein together, because neither is complete on its own and the pair is. 22 g protein per scoop, no dairy anywhere in the line. Plant protein is thicker than whey — mix it with more water than you think and give it a minute to settle.
usage: One scoop (32 g) in 300 ml water or oat drink. Let it stand for a minute before drinking.

name: Vegan Protein
short: Coconut, cinnamon and cardamom over a pea-rice base. Back in stock end of next week.
description: A chai-spiced plant protein with coconut through it, and it works hot as well as cold — stir it into oat milk on the stove and it drinks like a chai latte with 22 g of protein in it. Vegan, dairy-free, and currently sold out because we underestimated it twice in a row.
usage: One scoop (32 g) in 300 ml oat drink, cold or gently warmed. Do not boil it.

name: Casein Night
short: Slow protein for the last thing before bed. Thick, filling, 25 g per scoop.
description: Micellar casein digests over hours instead of minutes, so it is the shake for the evening rather than the one after training. It thickens as it stands — most people eat it with a spoon rather than drink it, which is not a defect.
usage: One scoop (32 g) in 200 ml milk, half an hour before bed. Less water if you want it as a pudding.

name: Clear Whey
short: Drinks like a cordial, not a milkshake. 20 g protein in a clear, cold glass.
description: Isolate built to stay clear in water — it comes out like iced tea instead of a shake. This is the one for people who cannot face something creamy in July, or after an hour of cardio. Light, tart, no dairy weight to it.
usage: One scoop (25 g) in 400 ml ice-cold water. Shake and let the foam drop before drinking.

name: Creatine Monohydrate
short: Three grams a day, a hundred days, fifteen euro. The most proven thing we sell.
description: Micronised creatine monohydrate, unflavoured, nothing added. It is the single best-studied supplement in sport and also one of the cheapest, which is a rare combination. No loading phase needed — take 3 to 5 g every day, including rest days, and be patient for three weeks.
usage: 3 to 5 g daily in any drink, any time of day. Consistency matters more than timing.

name: Creatine Monohydrate
short: Half a year of creatine in one tub. The size most people buy second.
description: 500 g of micronised monohydrate — 166 servings, about twelve cents a day. Same powder as the 300 g tub, better price per gram. Micronised means it sinks into water instead of floating on top of it.
usage: 3 to 5 g daily, every day. Mix into your shake, coffee or juice.

name: Creatine Monohydrate bulk
short: A kilo. Nearly a year at 3 g a day, at ten cents a serving.
description: The bulk bag of monohydrate for people who have decided creatine is permanent. 333 servings, resealable, keeps for two years in a dry cupboard. There is no version of creatine that works better than this — there are only more expensive ones.
usage: 3 to 5 g daily. A level scoop is 3 g; a heaped one is not a measurement.

name: Creapure Creatine
short: German-made Creapure, batch-tested. Buy it if the paperwork matters to you.
description: Creapure is monohydrate made in Germany to a tighter purity spec, with a certificate of analysis per batch. Chemically it does the same job as our standard monohydrate. It is here because tested athletes and careful people ask for it by name, and they should be able to buy it.
usage: 3 to 5 g daily, every day, in any liquid.

name: Creatine Gummies
short: 3 g of creatine in three chews. For the days a shaker is not happening.
description: Three gummies give you 3 g of creatine monohydrate — the same dose as a scoop, in a form that survives a rucksack and a work day. They cost more per gram than powder and we will not pretend otherwise; you are paying for the fact that you will actually take them while travelling.
usage: Three gummies a day, with or without food. Keep them out of a hot car.

name: Creatine Monohydrate
short: Creatine that tastes of something, for people who take it in water alone.
description: Monohydrate with a light lemon flavour, for the many people who take creatine in plain water and quietly hate it. 5 g of creatine per scoop, sweetened with sucralose. If you already mix yours into a shake, buy the unflavoured one and save four euro.
usage: One scoop (5 g) in 300 ml cold water, daily.

name: Creatine HCl caps
short: Capsules, no measuring, no taste. Four a day.
description: Creatine hydrochloride in capsules. More soluble than monohydrate and easier on some stomachs; the evidence that it outperforms monohydrate is thin, so buy it for the format, not for a promise. Four capsules is a full daily dose.
usage: Four capsules daily with water, any time of day.

name: Creatine Monohydrate value bag
short: Two kilos, 666 servings, eight cents a day. Split it with a training partner.
description: The largest creatine we stock. At 3 g a day it lasts nearly two years, which is longer than the best-before date on the bag — so this one is for a household, a gym floor or a group order. Same micronised monohydrate as every other tub on this page.
usage: 3 to 5 g daily. Decant a month at a time into a smaller tub and keep the bag sealed.

name: Pre-Workout Shock
short: 300 mg caffeine, 6 g citrulline, 3,2 g beta-alanine. Do not take it at nine at night.
description: A full-dose pre-workout: 300 mg caffeine, 6 g L-citrulline for blood flow, 3,2 g beta-alanine, 2 g tyrosine. Everything is dosed at the amount the studies used, which is why a serving is 12 g and not 5 g. The beta-alanine tingle is normal and harmless.
usage: One scoop (12 g) in 300 ml water, 20 minutes before training. Start with half a scoop the first time.

name: Pre-Workout Shock
short: Same full dose, softer flavour. 300 mg caffeine per scoop.
description: Watermelon Pre-Workout Shock — identical formula to the blue raspberry, easier to drink if you find sour flavours hard work first thing. 300 mg caffeine, 6 g citrulline, 3,2 g beta-alanine, 30 servings.
usage: One scoop (12 g) in 300 ml water, 20 minutes before training.

name: Pre-Workout Shock
short: Sold out. The cola batch goes faster than we plan for, every single time.
description: Cola Pre-Workout Shock: 300 mg caffeine, 6 g citrulline, 3,2 g beta-alanine, and the flavour everyone asks for in January. It is out of stock again. The watermelon and blue raspberry are the same formula if you cannot wait.
usage: One scoop (12 g) in 300 ml water, 20 minutes before training.

name: Pump Non-Stim
short: All the pump, none of the caffeine. For evening sessions and people who sleep badly.
description: 8 g of citrulline malate and 2,5 g of glycerol, with no stimulants at all. Train at nine in the evening and still sleep at eleven. Stack it with a coffee if you want the stimulant back, and skip the double-caffeine mistake of pairing it with a normal pre-workout.
usage: One scoop (16 g) in 400 ml water, 30 minutes before training. Drink plenty on top of it.

name: Pure Pre-Workout
short: Four ingredients, printed on the front. No sweetener, no colour, no aroma.
description: Caffeine, citrulline, beta-alanine, tyrosine. Nothing else — no sucralose, no dye, no flavour system to hide behind. It tastes sour and slightly bitter, which is what those four things taste like. People who use it do so precisely because there is nothing else in the tub.
usage: One scoop (12 g) in 400 ml water or juice, 20 minutes before training. Juice helps.

name: Beta-Alanine
short: 3,2 g a day, taken daily, for sets that last longer than a minute.
description: Beta-alanine works by building up in the muscle over weeks, so it does not matter when you take it — only that you take it every day. Useful for the 60-to-240 second efforts: rowing pieces, long sets, intervals. The skin tingle after a dose is harmless.
usage: 3,2 g daily, split into two doses if the tingle bothers you. Every day, training or not.

name: Citrulline Malate
short: 8 g of pure citrulline malate. Build your own pre-workout with it.
description: One ingredient, in the 2:1 ratio the research uses: 8 g per serving. This is the cheapest way to get the pump part of a pre-workout without paying for a flavour system and a stimulant you may not want. Very sour on its own.
usage: 8 g in 400 ml water or juice, 30 minutes before training.

name: Pre-Workout Lite
short: 100 mg caffeine instead of 300. New this month, and barely reviewed yet.
description: A third of the caffeine of Pre-Workout Shock, with the citrulline and beta-alanine left at full dose. It is for the morning trainer who already had two coffees, and for anyone who found a full pre-workout unpleasant rather than useful. Launched four weeks ago, so the reviews are still thin.
usage: One scoop (12 g) in 300 ml water, 20 minutes before training.
